questions.stem: Which of the following is an irrational number?
questions.explanation: $\sqrt{5}$ is irrational because 5 is not a perfect square, so its decimal expansion is non-terminating and non-repeating. The other options are all rational numbers.

questions.stem: Which statement about natural numbers is correct?

options.text: Natural numbers include negative whole numbers
Natural numbers start at 1 and include all positive whole numbers

questions.explanation: Natural numbers (counting numbers) are $1, 2, 3, 4, \ldots$ They start at 1 and do not include zero, negative numbers, or fractions.

questions.stem: The number $-7$ belongs to which of the following sets?

options.text: Natural numbers, integers, and rational numbers
Whole numbers, integers, and rational numbers
Integers, rational numbers, and real numbers

questions.explanation: $-7$ is negative, so it is not a natural number or whole number. It is an integer (whole number, positive or negative), a rational number (can be written as $\frac{-7}{1}$), and a real number.

options.text: Because its decimal expansion is recurring (repeating)
Because it contains only digits 1 to 7

questions.explanation: A number is rational if it can be written as a fraction of integers. All recurring decimals can be expressed as fractions, so $0.\overline{142857} = \frac{1}{7}$ is rational.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes the relationship between number sets?

options.text: All irrational numbers are rational numbers
All natural numbers are rational numbers

questions.explanation: Every natural number $n$ can be written as $\frac{n}{1}$, making it rational. The sets are nested: Natural $\subset$ Whole $\subset$ Integers $\subset$ Rational $\subset$ Real.

questions.stem: Classify $\sqrt{36}$. Which is the most complete correct answer?

options.text: Natural number, whole number, integer, rational number, and real number
Rational number and real number only

questions.explanation: $\sqrt{36} = 6$, which is a natural number (and therefore also a whole number, integer, rational number, and real number).

questions.stem: Which of the following is TRUE about $\pi$?

options.text: $\pi$ is a rational number because it can be approximated by fractions
$\pi$ is irrational because its decimal expansion never terminates and never repeats

questions.explanation: $\pi$ is irrational because its decimal expansion ($3.14159265\ldots$) goes on forever without repeating. $\frac{22}{7}$ is only an approximation of $\pi$, not its exact value.
